limitations: One developer machine (Windows, i7-6700HQ, 60 Hz, device scale factor 1), not an isolated host. Figures are this machine's, not a fleet's.
The 10,000-event workload is a stress case, not a size any lesson in the repository reaches.
Forced style/layout is measured by a layout read issued right after the call; it is what the browser must do synchronously there, not a full frame's rendering cost.

Paint, layerize and raster figures come only from the DevTools trace, taken on a separate page load with tracing on. Tracing adds overhead, so those figures are attributions of where frame time went, not clean durations comparable to the untraced samples.
Raster runs on worker threads and is attributed to the frame in which it starts; it may be finishing an earlier frame's work.
Long-task attribution from Chrome is 'unknown' with a 'window' container for every entry observed; no task is attributed to a script or element.
A long task that starts in one retained delta and ends after the next frame timestamp is recorded as spanning deltas and is not assigned to either.

Memory: Performance.getMetrics JS heap after a forced collection, and DOM node counts. The JS heap figure evidently excludes the DOM's own storage -- about 100,000 added nodes move it by under 1 MB -- so the byte cost of the DOM trees is not measured.
Active updates were measured with an eight-id window advancing one event per sample; how often the product issues active updates during playback was not measured.

decisions.name: Every animation frame repositions every fretboard note
decisions.finding: At 100 notes the loop holds 60 Hz: renderFrame() JavaScript median 0.26 ms, forced style/layout 0.92 ms, frame delta median 16.66 ms. At 1,000 the page falls to 30 Hz: frame delta median 33.32 ms while renderFrame() JavaScript is only 1.10 ms and forced style/layout 5.77 ms; the trace puts a median 14.4 ms of Paint, 4.9 ms of PrePaint and 3.8 ms of Layerize in each frame. At 10,000 each frame takes about 400 ms (run 1 median 399.85 ms, run 2 416.47 ms), JavaScript is 6.71 ms and forced style/layout 37.75 ms, and the trace's per-frame median Layerize is 256.8 ms and Paint 124.2 ms. Every frame at 10,000 is a long task of roughly 400 ms with unknown attribution. The JavaScript figure agrees with MAS-PERF-001's stub (5.5 ms at 10,000); the browser work after it is what grows.
decisions.next_action: The strongest optimization candidate, and now for a measured reason: the cost is in paint and layerization of a moving tree of note elements, not in the loop. An authorized order should compare viewport culling against a transform-based canvas move with this harness as the before/after instrument, and re-run the DO-015 Stage 9 witness.

decisions.name: Active-state updates traverse the whole rendered score
decisions.finding: The full applyActiveEventIds() on a real SVG tree costs 0.22 / 1.16 / 8.19 ms (TAB) and 0.16 / 1.53 / 13.66 ms (notation) at 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 events. The selector alone, measured in its own frames, costs 0.02 / 0.13 / 1.03 ms (TAB) and 0.06 / 0.50 / 5.09 ms (notation): it is the smaller part at every size. MAS-PERF-001's stub loop (0.679 ms at 10,000) was a low floor; the real per-element attribute read and class toggle over every group is what costs. Style/layout forced after an update stays small (at most 3.2 ms at 10,000).
decisions.next_action: Before any change, measure how often playback issues an active update. If it is per active-set change, 1,000 events costs under 2 ms per view and can wait; at 10,000 an id-to-element map built at mount, touching only the ids that changed, addresses the loop rather than the selector.

decisions.name: A mount serializes the whole score and replaces innerHTML
decisions.finding: Replacing the notation tree costs, per stage medians, 3.62 / 22.23 / 206.38 ms to build the string, 3.62 / 24.47 / 226.38 ms for the innerHTML replacement, and 5.39 / 25.30 / 214.90 ms of forced style/layout at 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 events; TAB is 2.10 / 14.28 / 92.99, 2.08 / 14.71 / 123.17 and 2.86 / 19.08 / 174.73 ms. The two browser stages MAS-PERF-001 could not see are each as large as the string build it measured (241.7 ms at 10,000 in Node, 206.4 ms here). The trace shows ParseHTML at 354.5 ms for both views at 10,000.
decisions.next_action: A mount happens on lesson load, not per frame: at 1,000 events it is a noticeable pause, at 10,000 a freeze of well over half a second per view. Avoiding the string alone would address one stage of three; an authorized change should target the number of elements mounted (windowed rendering of measures) and be measured with this harness.

decisions.name: Paint and compositing of the fretboard frame
decisions.finding: The trace decoded at every size and is attributable per frame: frames are cut at the page's own FireAnimationFrame events inside user-timing marks, warm-ups dropped. Per-frame medians: Paint 1.64 / 14.40 / 124.24 ms, PrePaint 0.48 / 4.85 / 42.40 ms, Layerize 0.24 / 3.83 / 256.81 ms at 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 notes. Paint is the largest stage at 1,000 and Layerize at 10,000. Raster started per frame stays under 1 ms. These are trace-clock figures under tracing overhead, on a separate page load; they locate the cost and are not added to or subtracted from the sampled numbers.
decisions.next_action: Treat as the explanation for M2 rather than a separate fix: whichever M2 change is authorized should be judged on these per-frame stages as well as on frame deltas.

decisions.name: Memory held by mounted views and the fretboard
decisions.finding: Measured reliably: after a forced collection, mounting both score views adds 1,033 / 10,001 / 99,718 DOM nodes and the fretboard 431 / 4,032 / 40,032 at 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 events, while the JS heap grows by at most about 1 MB. That heap figure evidently excludes the DOM's own storage -- 99,718 nodes moved it by 0.6 MB -- so the byte cost of the trees is not captured by the metric the browser exposes reliably here.
decisions.next_action: If memory becomes a question, measure with a heap snapshot including native DOM size, or performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory() on this cross-origin-isolated page; node counts alone already scale linearly and would fall with any M2 or M5 windowing.
